migration.migration_reason: Legacy support adjudication is derived deterministically from the already current-validator-approved canonical owner records. No new model judgment or score is introduced.

C++.justification: `using Shape = std::variant<Circle,Rect>; Shape s = Circle{2.0};` — std::variant (C++17) is a closed alternative set fixed at the type's declaration; no code elsewhere can add a third alternative to this Shape alias.

Go.justification: Go has no native closed sum/variant type. Named substitution (R9): a 'sealed interface' pattern (an interface with an unexported method) approximates closedness within the compilation unit; construction of a Circle literal bound to the Shape interface value satisfies the rest.

Java.justification: sealed interface Shape permits Circle, Rect {} ; record Circle(double r) implements Shape {} ; record Rect(double w, double h) implements Shape {} — sealed hierarchy is a closed alternative set enforced by the compiler (Java 17+ sealed classes).

Kotlin.justification: sealed class Shape; data class Circle(val r: Double): Shape(); data class Rect(val w: Double, val h: Double): Shape() — Kotlin sealed classes are compiler-enforced closed to the same module (cannot be subclassed from outside).

Python.justification: Python has no closed-sum-type declaration; a class hierarchy or dataclass union is the nearest standard substitute, but nothing in the language prevents a third case being added elsewhere, per R9 named substitution.

Quidra.citation: language.md 'Named enums and variants': enums are a closed, exhaustively-matched set of variants each carrying at most one explicitly typed payload; a two-field Rect payload is expressed as a small payload class, which is a natural composition rather than a substitution of the closedness mechanism being tested.
Quidra.fragment:
class RectData
    float w
    float h

enum Shape
    Circle(float)
    Rect(RectData)

Shape s = Shape.Circle(2.0)
Quidra.justification: language.md 'Named enums and variants': enums are a closed, exhaustively-matched set of variants each carrying at most one explicitly typed payload; a two-field Rect payload is expressed as a small payload class, which is a natural composition rather than a substitution of the closedness mechanism being tested.

Rust.fragment:
enum Shape { Circle { r: f64 }, Rect { w: f64, h: f64 } }
let s: Shape = Shape::Circle { r: 2.0 };

Swift.justification: enum Shape { case circle(r: Double); case rect(w: Double, h: Double) } — enum is a closed, exhaustively-checked sum type; language rules forbid adding a case from elsewhere.

TypeScript.fragment:
type Shape = { kind: "circle"; r: number } | { kind: "rect"; w: number; h: number };
const s: Shape = { kind: "circle", r: 2.0 };
TypeScript.justification: type Shape = {kind:'Circle', r:number} | {kind:'Rect', w:number, h:number}; discriminated union, closed by declaration; const s: Shape = {kind:'Circle', r:2.0};

Zig.fragment:
const Shape = union(enum) { Circle: struct{r:f64}, Rect: struct{w:f64,h:f64} };
const s: Shape = .{.Circle = .{.r=2.0}};
Zig.justification: union(enum) { Circle: f64, Rect: struct{w:f64,h:f64} } is a closed, exhaustive tagged union; the compiler forbids adding a case elsewhere.
